description: Ateso is an Eastern Nilotic language spoken by about two and a half million people in eastern Uganda, around Soroti, Kumi, Serere and Amuria, and by the Iteso of western Kenya.
notes: Drafted by Claude (AI) for the Ateso courses (#131) with low confidence in Ateso; needs a native-speaker review.

why.title: The language of **Soroti, Kumi and the lakes of Teso.**
why.text: Ateso belongs to the Ateker family with Karimojong and Turkana, so it opens a whole group of languages from Uganda to Kenya and South Sudan. Learn it for family, travel, work, and the songs, dances and stories of Teso.

cards.title: For family
cards.text: Talk with grandparents and relatives in Soroti and Kumi.

cards.title: For travellers
cards.text: Find your way from Soroti to Kumi, Ngora and Lake Bisina.

cards.title: For the curious
cards.text: Meet a Nilotic language with gendered nouns, verb prefixes and no noun classes.

landing.farewell: Eyalama noi — thank you very much.
landing.audience: Complete beginners, families from Teso, volunteers and travellers heading to eastern Uganda.
landing.first: Greetings, introductions and numbers, then family, food, the market, time, places, the home and health, unit by unit.

cast.emma: A visitor learning Ateso before her trip
